Filed Against The Petitioner/Accused No.5 In
C.C.No.5297/2015 Pending On The File Of Iii Acmm Court
At Bangalore For Offences Punishable U/S.498A Read
With 34 Of Ipc And Section 3 And 4 Of Dowry
Prohibition Act.
 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The present petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. deserves to be allowed and the proceedings for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, is liable to be quashed in the light of settlement arrived between respondent No.2-complainant and her husband.

2. It is borne out from the records that serious allegations were made against accused Nos.1 to 4 who are husband, mother-in-law, sister-in-law and brother-in-law respectively of respondent No.2-complainant.
Accused No.5 admittedly is a distant relative and nowhere concerned with the alleged offence.

If respondent No.2- wife has arrived at a settlement with her husband against whom these allegations are made, then I am of the view NC: 2023:KHC:20718 that the proceedings are liable to be quashed even against the petitioner-accused No.5.
3.

On perusal of the order passed by the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.123/2019, it is forthcoming at para 7 of the said order that respondent No.2 has agreed to take Rs.12,00,000/-
towards full and final settlement and a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- is already paid by accused No.1 by way of Demand Draft.
It is in this background, this Court would find that respondent No.2 has not chosen to contest this proceedings.

If the proceedings under Section 498(A) and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act are quashed against husband, then I am of the view that the proceedings cannot be allowed to be continued against the petitioner herein who is only a distant relative and if proceedings are not quashed would amount to abuse of process.
4. I have taken cognizance of the nature and gravity of offences alleged in the instant case on hand.

A crime is registered on account of matrimonial dispute NC: 2023:KHC:20718 between husband,
wife and in-laws.
Admittedly, the alleged offences are not heinous and serious offences.

The offences, on account of matrimonial dispute, subsequently having amended in an amicable settlement between husband, wife and in-laws, the decision to continue with trial in such cases, in all probability, leads to miscarriage of justice.
Therefore, I am more than satisfied that this is a fit case to quash the proceedings even against accused No.5.
Therefore, to meet the ends of justice, the proceedings pending in C.C.No.5297/2015 are liable to be quashed.

5. For the reasons stated supra, I pass the following:
